pull.title: subprocess: fix command line memory leak on Windows
pull.body:
`Popen::execute_process()` copied the command line into a buffer from `new[]`, but did not delete it. This leaked memory each time a process started on Windows.

`CreateProcessA` [needs](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/processthreadsapi/nf-processthreadsapi-createprocessa#:~:text=characters%2E-,The,violation) a writable command line buffer. Since C++17, `std::string::data()` supplies one, so give the `std::string` buffer directly and remove the copy.

This only affects Windows. It is only reachable if `-signer=<cmd>` is set, through authenticated RPC or the GUI. Each call leaks only the startup-defined `<cmd>`, and the rate is limited by process spawn time, so the impact is limited.

_edit: this was fixed upstream in https://github.com/arun11299/cpp-subprocess/pull/131, but since this codebase is C++20 it seems better to avoid the copy (and the const cast). A direct backport isn't possible anyway, since #35704 switched us to CreateProcessA._

Has this patch been checked on a windows box? I find the null terminator behaviour hard to reason about.

You mean outside the Windows CI, which covers `rpc_singer.py`?

https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/actions/runs/39405290402/job/118569619457?pr=36581#step:14:1185 and https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/actions/runs/39405290402/job/118571318163?pr=36581#step:11:418 


Maybe there could be a  Windows `/fsanitize=address` nightly build with leak sanitizer enabled as well?

Took it for a spin in a Windows debug build now (had not previously done so). Overriding through: ````c++ command_line = "C:\\Users\\hodlinator\\bitcoin\\build\\bin\\Debug\\bitcoind.exe arg"; ```` There was no null terminator inserted/overwritten for that string:

Ran it again and set a memory breakpoint on the space-char before "arg", but it didn't fire, so it wasn't temporarily replaced with NUL and then set back to space (as far as the debugger could observe, I confirmed it would break when our code modified memory).

Thanks for the empirical data, @hodlinator! Also, `command_line` is a local variable and unused after the `CreateProcessA` call, and the buffer `CreateProcessA` receives is the same as before - just with a different owner.

ACK fe6608590c624042fa4a77a6c9f3a46b70bc646c.

Consider https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/36581#discussion_r4348776404 as a nit.

events.body: Force-pushed to remove [an unnecessary docstring change](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/36581#discussion_r4349723923), no other changes.

comments.diff_hunk:
@@ -1121,7 +1118,7 @@ inline void Popen::execute_process() noexcept(false)
 
   // Create the child process.
   bSuccess = CreateProcessA(NULL,
-                            szCmdline,    // command line
+                            command_line.data(), // command line; must be writable (LPSTR)
comments.body:
https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/processthreadsapi/nf-processthreadsapi-createprocessa states:
> The system adds a terminating null character to the command-line string to separate the file name from the arguments. This divides the original string into two strings for internal processing.

But that should be fine as I interpret it as the *replacement* of a `char`-value, and this is the last place `command_line` is used.

   // Create the child process.
   bSuccess = CreateProcessA(NULL,
-                            szCmdline,    // command line
+                            command_line.data(), // command line; must be writable (LPSTR)
comments.body:
The docs only state that **CreateProcessW** can modify the string. They don’t say either way for **CreateProcessA**.

So maybe no need to amend the code comment?

comments.body:
Ah, it's further up:

> The Unicode version of this function, **CreateProcessW**, can modify the contents of this string. Therefore, this parameter cannot be a pointer to read-only memory (such as a const variable or a literal string). If this parameter is a constant string, the function may cause an access violation.

-                            szCmdline,    // command line

comments.body: `CreateProcessA` requires a mutable string (`LPSTR`) as part of its function signature, and it [seems](https://devblogs.microsoft.com/oldnewthing/20090601-00/?p=18083/#:~:text=Why%20is,string%21) like the implementation then passes a copy to `CreateProcessW`. But I agree that perhaps the docstring change is confusing, `CreateProcessA`'s function signature is enough, what it does under the hood is not our concern. Force-pushed.
